import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 726

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/726](https://www.erdosproblems.com/726)
- [EGRS75] Erdős, P., and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., On the prime factors of
  $(\sp{2n}\sb{n})$. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
-/

open Nat Filter Finset
open scoped Topology Asymptotics

namespace Erdos726

/--
As $n\to \infty$ ranges over integers
$\sum_{p\leq n}1_{n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}}\frac{1}{p}\sim \frac{\log\log n}{2}$?

A conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75].

By $n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}$ we mean $n\equiv r\pmod{p}$ for some integer $r$ with $p/2<r<p$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_726 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (range (n + 1)).filter
          (fun p : ℕ ↦ p.Prime ∧ (p : ℝ) / 2 < (n % p : ℝ)),
        (1 : ℝ) / (p : ℝ))
      ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) / 2) := by
  sorry

/--
The classical estimate of Mertens states that $\sum_{p\leq n}\frac{1}{p}\sim \log\log n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_726.variants.mertens_estimate :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (range (n + 1)).filter (fun p ↦ p.Prime), (1 : ℝ) / ((p : ℕ) : ℝ))
    ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos726

findings.description: On line 45, `(n % p : ℝ)` elaborates as `(n : ℝ) % (p : ℝ)`, not as the cast of the natural-number remainder. Mathlib supplies real-field remainder through `Field.toEuclideanDomain`, where `a % b = a - a * b / b`. Consequently this remainder is zero for every prime p. The filter requires `p / 2 < 0` and is therefore empty for every n, so the sum is identically zero and the right-hand asymptotic claim is trivially false. For example, the source selects p = 3 at n = 5 because the integer remainder is 2; its sum is 1/3 there, whereas the Lean sum is zero. Both the filter's emptiness and the negation of the asymptotic were proved independently in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/726 states `∑_{p≤n} 1_{n∈(p/2,p) (mod p)} / p ∼ (log log n)/2`, explicitly defining the indicator condition by the existence of an integer r with `n ≡ r (mod p)` and `p/2 < r < p`. The cited EGRS75 paper, p. 90, likewise specifies primes for which `n = kp + r`, with `p/2 < r < p` and k integral: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-27.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `(n % p : ℝ)` with `((n % p : ℕ) : ℝ)`, forcing remainder to be evaluated in ℕ before coercion. The corrected filter predicate is `p.Prime ∧ (p : ℝ) / 2 < ((n % p : ℕ) : ℝ)`. For prime p, `Nat.mod_lt n hp.pos` supplies the upper bound on the remainder. The corrected sum's equality with the source's explicit integer-congruence indicator sum was verified in Lean.

sources_consulted: Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus, On the prime factors of binom(2n,n), Mathematics of Computation 29 (1975), 83–92, especially p. 90: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-27.pdf

Local Mathlib sources: Algebra/EuclideanDomain/{Field,Defs,Basic}.lean; Analysis/Asymptotics/{Defs,AsymptoticEquivalent}.lean; Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean; Data/Nat/Prime/Defs.lean; Data/Int/ModEq.lean; Data/Finset/{Range,Filter}.lean.
Local repository guidance and machinery: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, and FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean.
Supplied historical calibration: /workspace/past_misformalizations/INDEX.md, pr04290.md, pr01525.md, pr03884.md, and pr01642.md.
review.notes: Checked both declarations. The Mertens variant matches the source: its prime range and real reciprocals are correct, and small-input logarithm values are harmless at `atTop`. The website still records Problem 726 as open; the posted proof claim explicitly describes a conditional result, not an unconditional resolution. Source pages and the paper were read through r.jina.ai where needed. `/workspace/review/verified.lean` compiles successfully and proves the defect, the proposed correction's equivalence to the source sum, and the relevant boundary/asymptotic checks. Axiom inspection of the refutation and correction proof shows no `sorryAx`. All experiments were confined to `/workspace/review/`.

submission.summary: Replaced `(n % p : ℝ)` with `((n % p : ℕ) : ℝ)` so the remainder is computed in ℕ before being cast to ℝ. No other declarations, docstrings, or attributes were changed. The required compilation succeeds with only the existing `declaration uses sorry` warnings.
